paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: live API cost per chat, subagents, and the whole machine.
# dsh-api-cost
A DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle that shows **what the current session's API usage costs**, right be
side the token counter under the composer — and why.
English | 简体中文
## What it is
This repository is a **Harness plugin bundle**: one package that contributes a **Host plugin** and a
**Web Client plugin** to a Harness profile.
- The Host plugin registers a session projection (`apiCost`) that folds the provider-reported usage

of every settled model call into per-route billing buckets and prices them.
- The Client plugin regi
sters one control in the composer's ambient dock (`conversation.composer.dock`) and renders the valu
e the Host already computed.
It is **not** a skill (skills are model-facing instructions the Agent loads), **not** an agent prese
t (presets compose plugins for a session), and **not** a standalone app. A bundle is the unit the Ha
rness Plugin Manager installs, enables, and removes.
## What you see
Under the composer, after the built-in statistics:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Clicking the cost opens a small panel:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The total covers the whole conversation: this Session **plus every subagent session it delegated to*
*, with their share listed separately. The control reads each descendant's cost itself, so you never
have to open that conversation first; while a descendant is unread or still running, the total carr
ies a `+` to mark it as a floor or a provisional figure. Every completed turn also shows its own cos
t in the turn footer, next to the chat's token-usage entry (`本轮 ¥0.0123`).
The panel also switches to a **time range**: `Today`, `Last 24h`, `Last 7 days`, or `Last 30 days`,
totalling every stored session on the machine.
The control disappears while there is no billable usage, and an unrecognized `provider/model` is sho
wn as *No price configured* instead of being silently guessed.
## Install
Requirements: DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or another `0.2.x` release (`engines.dsh` is declared),
eepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or another `0.2.x` release (`engines.dsh` is declared), and the Web UI.
**From the Web UI:** open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Install**, and paste this repository'
Web UI:** open **Plugins** in the sidebar, choose **Install**, and paste this repository's address:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**From the CLI:**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**From an agent:** call `plugin_manager` with `action: install_bundle` and the same address (or a lo
cal checkout path while developing).
A Git install follows the branch head; pin a commit (`github:wei2yun/dsh-api-cost#<sha>`) when you n
eed a reproducible install. The package ships plain ESM, so a Git install runs no build script.
### Distribution
This repository is the bundle itself: no build step, no runtime dependency to install, and every fil
e the Host and the browser load is committed. It installs from a Git dependency, a local checkout, o
r npm if it is ever published there. Discovery follows the ecosystem's `dsh-plugin` GitHub topic; a
plugin-market index entry is optional and not required to install.
Then send a message. A page that was already open before the install has no baseline for the new pro
jection yet, so refresh once if the control does not appear immediately.
The plugin stores nothing and changes no Harness setting beyond its own profile entry. Remove it fro
m the Plugins page at any time.
## Time ranges
The range tabs add up **every session this Harness home has stored, across all workspaces** — the wh
ole machine's consumption under the configured API key, not just the conversation you are reading:
1. The Host reads the durable session store through `ctx.sessionPersistence` — no filesystem parsing

, no private paths.
2. Each session is folded into a compact per-call list (time, route, token bucke

ts), skipping a forked session's inherited prefix and keeping the last 35 days.
3. That list is cach

ed against the store's own `revision`, so a repeated query rereads only sessions that changed.
4. Ca
lls are summed exactly inside the half-open window and priced per call with the same book: `Today` s
tarts at local midnight, the others are rolling windows ending now.
The browser reads the result from the plugin's own same-origin route (`/plugins/api-cost/window`), w
hich answers aggregates only — no session ids, no content. The route is part of the Host half, so it
exists after the next Harness restart.
## Per-turn cost
Each `assistant/message` also folds into a table keyed by its turn number, so the completed-turn foo
ter can show what that turn cost. The turn chip reads the same projection value the panel does and d
isappears when the turn has no billable call (a compaction, for example, is billed to the session bu
t belongs to no turn).
## How the number is produced
1. Every settled model call appends an `assistant/message` event carrying the provider's `usage` and
the concrete `provider`/`model` route. The summarizer call behind a compaction appends the same fac
ts on `compaction/summary` and is billed like any other call. A streaming attempt is billed from its
streamed usage sample and then replaced by the settled message of the same turn and step; `llm/retr
y-started` closes that replacement slot, so a retried attempt is billed on its own — an aborted call

that never settles is still counted once the provider reported usage for it.
2. The projection fold
s those events into four disjoint buckets per route — uncached input, cache-hit input, cache-write i

nput, output — split by price period.
3. The Client-visible view prices the buckets with the list pr

ices below and publishes the total, the per-route breakdown, and the peak/off-peak split.
4. The con
trol adds the `apiCost` of every descendant session (`origin: subagent`). When the session list does
not carry that value yet — a freshly spawned child, or a checkpoint written before this plugin exis
ted — the control asks the session controller to fold the descendant's projections on demand, withou
t opening that conversation. A forked child inherits the parent's log, so its `inherited` share is s
ubtracted and only what the fork itself spent is counted. A child that is still running is read agai
n once it settles, so a mid-run snapshot never becomes the final number.
Because the Session log stays the only source of truth, replay, resume, and fork derive the same num
ber, and the plugin never writes to the log.
